trigger.source: must be computed from tracker-level state

firing_rule.condition: switch when B_pending <= B_switch with B_switch = N * S0
semantics: if the condition is false, allocate using the current S
if the condition is true and the run has not switched yet, perform the single allowed switch
the target S governs all subsequently allocated ranges
once switched, S remains fixed for the remainder of the run

edge_cases.below_threshold_before_first_allocation: if B_pending is already below the threshold before the first allocation, the switch occurs at that allocation boundary
edge_cases.eof_before_threshold_evaluation: if EOF occurs before the threshold is evaluated, no switch occurs
edge_cases.no_allocation_after_crossing: if no allocation occurs after the threshold is crossed, no artificial switch event is created
edge_cases.in_flight_bytes: InFlightBytes includes currently allocated but incomplete ranges according to tracker state
edge_cases.retries: retries preserve original range boundaries and do not retroactively resize ranges
edge_cases.sampling: CompletedBytes / InFlightBytes must be sampled from tracker-level state immediately before the allocation decision

evaluation_semantics.evaluation_point: evaluated exactly once per allocation decision on the downloader's serialized allocation path, immediately before the RangeTracker is asked to allocate a new range and before any tracker state mutation for that allocation
evaluation_semantics.completed_bytes_sampling: sampled at the evaluation point from the tracker-level completed-bytes counter; a range contributes only after its completion is recorded (assembler write acknowledged and tracker marked complete); the counter is monotone non-decreasing within a run
evaluation_semantics.in_flight_bytes_sampling: sampled at the same evaluation instant as the sum of the original byte lengths of all ranges in the tracker's in-flight set (allocated to the worker pool, not yet complete); in-flight ranges are never resized
evaluation_semantics.retry_treatment: a failed range leaves the in-flight set with its original boundaries preserved; its bytes are neither completed nor in-flight and re-enter B_pending until reallocated; a retry re-enters the in-flight set with the original boundaries and never re-splits the range
evaluation_semantics.allocation_completion_ordering: allocation, completion, and failure transitions are serialized on the tracker path; the two samples are taken at the same evaluation instant and are consistent; the candidate new range is not counted in either sample before allocation
evaluation_semantics.relative_to_allocation: the trigger is evaluated immediately before new range allocation; a fired switch changes the chunk-size target for the allocation that follows (future allocations only) and never touches in-flight requests
evaluation_semantics.post_switch_rule: after the switch, the chunk size remains fixed for the remainder of the run
evaluation_semantics.no_switch_case: if the trigger never fires, the run completes at the starting chunk size

rule.text: GO iff ALL of the following hold; otherwise NO-GO: (1) mechanism presence: for every fixed chunk-size arm, pooled median per-request service time within +/-25% of D + s/R; (2) direction: median_service_time(256 KiB) < median_service_time(1 MiB) < median_service_time(4 MiB) < median_service_time(16 MiB); (3) tail sufficiency: pooled median realized 16 MiB tail >= 20 s AND within [0.8*T_tail_primary, 1.25*T_tail_primary]; (4) feasibility/reliability: >= 28/32 clean runs, <= 30 minutes wall-clock per run, within-block residual SD of log(T/T_ref) <= 0.25
